hints: First factor out the coefficient of $x^2$ from the terms involving $x$, then complete the square.
walkthrough:
Factor out $2$ from the first two terms and complete the square:
$$2x^2 - 12x + 11 = 2(x^2 - 6x) + 11 = 2\left[(x - 3)^2 - 9\right] + 11$$
$$= 2(x - 3)^2 - 18 + 11 = 2(x - 3)^2 - 7$$
where $a = 2, b = -3, c = -7$.

hints: The vertex is at $x = 3$, so largest $k = 3$.
walkthrough:
The quadratic function has its minimum turning point at $x = 3$.
For $f$ to be a one-to-one strictly decreasing function on $x \le k$, the domain must be bounded by the vertex:
$$\text{Largest value of } k = 3$$

hints: Range of $f$ on $x \le 3$ is $f(x) \ge -7 \implies$ Domain of $f^{-1}$ is $x \ge -7$.
walkthrough:
Set $y = 2(x - 3)^2 - 7$ and isolate $x$ for the domain $x \le 3$ (where $x - 3 \le 0$):
$$2(x - 3)^2 = y + 7 \implies (x - 3)^2 = \frac{y + 7}{2}$$
$$x - 3 = -\sqrt{\frac{y + 7}{2}} \implies x = 3 - \sqrt{\frac{y + 7}{2}}$$
$$f^{-1}(x) = 3 - \sqrt{\frac{x + 7}{2}}$$

Determine the domain of $f^{-1}$ from the range of $f$ on $x \le 3$:
$$\text{Domain of } f^{-1}: \quad x \ge -7 \quad (\text{or } [-7, \infty))$$

hints: For $fg(x)$ to exist with $k = 1$, we need $g(x) \le 1 \implies x + 3 \le 1 \implies x \le -2$, so largest $p = -2$.
walkthrough:
For the composite function $fg(x) = f(g(x))$ to be defined with domain of $f$ restricted by $k = 1$ ($u \le 1$):
$$\text{Range}(g) \subseteq \text{Domain}(f) \implies x + 3 \le 1 \implies x \le -2$$
$$\text{Largest value of } p = -2$$
